CS3.note: the execution client has no notion of an SRW3-invalid block: it builds and VALIDates a child of the rejected payload; only the CL-side simulated rule prevents extension

analysis.latestValidHashSemantics: client returns latestValidHash=parent for an execution-VALID payload; an SRW3-INVALID translation would overload INVALID with a NON-execution validity notion (see report section 15)
analysis.forkchoiceSemantics: the CL must treat the SRW3-rejected head as nonexistent; forkchoice then never extends it; identical policy required across all clients or branches diverge
analysis.reorgConsequence: if any client lacks the policy, it will extend the rejected branch, producing a persistent fork: SRW3 enforcement at this boundary is a fork-choice rule, not a validity rule
